title: Anuparna Roy Returns to Venice With Mumbai Migration Drama 'Lovers in the Blue Night'
excerpt: The West Bengal filmmaker, who won Best Director at Venice's Orizzonti section last year, becomes one of the few Indian directors with two consecutive films in competition at the festival.
body:
• Anuparna Roy's second feature Lovers in the Blue Night will premiere on September 11 in the Orizzonti competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival.
  • Roy won Best Director in the same section last year for her debut Songs of Forgotten Trees, making her the first Indian filmmaker to earn the honour.
  • The multilingual drama follows four migrants in Mumbai navigating love, identity and survival, told in Hindi, Sylheti, Bengali and Marathi.
  • A US-India co-production, the film is produced by Khan & Kumar Media and sold internationally by Parallax.

Indian filmmaker Anuparna Roy is heading back to the Venice Lido. Her second feature, Lovers in the Blue Night, has been selected for the Orizzonti competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, where it will have its world premiere on September 11.

The selection makes Roy one of the very few Indian filmmakers to have two consecutive features premiere in competition at Venice — a milestone for independent Indian cinema. Last year, her debut Songs of Forgotten Trees earned her the Best Director award in the same section, making her the first Indian director to receive that honour.

A Story Rooted in Memory

Set against the restless pulse of Mumbai's nightlife, Lovers in the Blue Night follows four migrants — a closeted husband, his lonely wife who works in a bar, a small-time thief and a pimp — whose lives become intertwined through unexpected love, survival and forbidden desire. The film explores loneliness, caste, migration, sexuality and the human search for belonging.

https://x.com/Variety/status/2097204560506859630

“The film draws from my own life as a migrant, watching working-class lives slowly dissolve into the restless pulse of the city. It is about people who dare to desire in a world that punishes feelings.”

— Anuparna Roy, Director

Roy, who was born in Narayanpur, a village in the Purulia district of West Bengal, has spoken about the deeply personal origins of the film. She has said one character was inspired by a woman named Ameena, a bonded labourer from her hometown. “I innocently asked her why she and her husband Karim never slept together. She quietly replied, 'He doesn't take me with him,'” Roy recalled, according to Cinema Express. “Through this film, I wanted to carry that memory into an imagined Mumbai, where Ameena chooses her own freedom and desire.”

A Multilingual Ensemble

Told in Hindi with Sylheti, Bengali and Marathi, the film features an ensemble cast including Neelima Sharma, Pritam Pilania, Bhushan Shimpi, Jatin Sarin, Kajal Keshav and Vinod Suryavanshi. Lead actress Neelima Sharma told Indulge Express that her character is from Assam, requiring her to learn a new language. “It's also a language that is slowly becoming extinct, which is why Anuparna wanted to retain it,” Sharma said.

The film is a co-production between the United States and India, produced by Vikas Kumar and Sharib Khan at Khan & Kumar Media, along with Bibhanshu Rai, Romil Modi and Rhet Topham. International sales are handled by Parallax.

From Call Centre to the Venice Lido

Roy's trajectory is itself a remarkable story. She studied English literature at Kulti College under Burdwan University before working in a call centre in Delhi and as an IT sales executive in Mumbai. She entered the film industry in 2023 as an assistant director on Run to the River, and within two years had directed a Venice award winner.

Expressing gratitude over the selection, Roy said, according to Hollywood Reporter India: “Returning to the Orizzonti Competition is both humbling and deeply emotional. I'm deeply thankful to the Venice programming team for believing in our film.” She added that she hoped the recognition would “encourage more honest, fearless, and deeply human stories to find their audience.”

What to Watch

The 83rd Venice International Film Festival runs from September 2 to 12, with American filmmaker Maggie Gyllenhaal serving as Jury President for the main competition. Lovers in the Blue Night joins a lineup that includes films from Lee Chang-Dong, Hirokazu Koreeda and Shinya Tsukamoto. Roy's premiere on September 11 will be closely watched as one of the festival's most anticipated independent entries.
